rules.text: Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines and move detailed reference material into separate files.
rules.why: Anthropic's skills docs: "Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines. Move detailed reference material to separate files."

rules.text: Write the description to say what the skill does and when to use it, with the key use case first and keywords people would naturally say.
rules.why: Claude uses the description to decide when to apply the skill; if a skill triggers too often, the docs advise making the description more specific.

rules.text: Keep descriptions short: the combined description and when_to_use text is cut at 1,536 characters, and when many skills overflow the listing budget (1% of the context window) some descriptions are dropped.
rules.why: A dropped description removes the keywords Claude needs to match your request.

rules.text: Give every SKILL.md frontmatter with a name and a complete description of what the skill does and when to use it.
rules.why: The reference skills repository requires exactly these two frontmatter fields.

rules.text: Set disable-model-invocation: true on skills with side effects, such as deploying or pushing, so they only run when you invoke them.
rules.why: Anthropic's best-practices page recommends it for workflows you want to trigger manually.

rules.text: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file and move instructions that only matter for part of the codebase into path-scoped rules.
rules.why: Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.

rules.text: For each CLAUDE.md line ask whether removing it would cause Claude to make mistakes; if not, cut it.
rules.why: Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions.

rules.text: Use a hook, not a CLAUDE.md line, for anything that must happen every time.
rules.why: Claude treats CLAUDE.md as context, not enforced configuration; hooks are deterministic.

rules.text: Reference secrets in .mcp.json as ${VAR} environment variables instead of writing the values in the file.
rules.why: Claude Code expands ${VAR} in .mcp.json so teams can share a config while keeping API keys out of it.

rules.text: Reference sensitive values such as API keys in .mcp.json with ${VAR} environment variable expansion instead of writing them into the file.
rules.why: The MCP docs say ${VAR} expansion lets teams share configurations while keeping machine-specific paths and sensitive values like API keys flexible.

rules.text: Point remote MCP servers at https:// URLs; HTTP-transport servers are the recommended option and SSE is deprecated.
rules.why: MCP OAuth credentials are only sent to token endpoints over HTTPS (or localhost), so sign-in fails against plain http:// elsewhere.

rules.text: Only connect MCP servers you wrote or that come from providers you trust.
rules.why: Anthropic does not security-audit or manage MCP servers, and servers that fetch external content can expose you to prompt injection.

rules.text: Commit .claude/settings.json only for what the whole team shares, and keep personal settings in .claude/settings.local.json.
rules.why: Everyone who clones the repository gets the committed .claude/settings.json; settings.local.json is for your personal overrides in one project and is kept out of git.

rules.text: Put personal, per-project overrides in .claude/settings.local.json so teammates are unaffected.
rules.why: Project local settings sit above shared project settings and are for personal overrides for one project.

rules.text: Add deny rules such as Read(./.env) and Read(./.env.*) to block access to secret files.
rules.why: The settings docs show these as the example deny rules for environment files.

rules.text: Avoid allow rules like Bash(*) or a bare Bash; allow specific commands such as Bash(git log *) instead.
rules.why: Bash(*) is equivalent to Bash and matches every Bash command; the docs recommend putting the * after the subcommand to limit a rule.

rules.text: Do not rely on Bash allow rules to restrict command arguments or URLs; use a sandbox or a hook for that.
rules.why: The permissions docs warn that Bash patterns constraining arguments, such as Bash(curl http://github.com/ *), are fragile and miss variations.

rules.text: Make sure every hook command points at a script that exists and is executable (chmod +x), and reference it with an absolute path or "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR".
rules.why: "command not found" and silently non-running hooks are the first two troubleshooting items in the hooks guide.

rules.text: Use hooks for actions that must happen every time with zero exceptions, such as blocking edits to .env or lockfiles.
rules.why: Unlike CLAUDE.md instructions, which are advisory, hooks are deterministic.

rules.text: Disable plugins you do not use; every enabled plugin adds its skill and agent descriptions to context on every turn.
rules.why: Those tokens count toward usage even in sessions where nothing from the plugin runs.

rules.text: Review a plugin before installing it: it can run code with your user privileges, whichever marketplace it came from.
rules.why: Anthropic's plugin docs state this for all three marketplace tiers.
